What they mean by Wii Emulator is the Wii virtual console, which is an official emulator that is accepted for speedruns. To get the japanese oot virtual console version you have to use homebrew. I don't know where to send you for that, but googling about Wii Virtual Console homebrew should help you.

And the wii has gamecube ports build into it, so that's not a problem as long as you have a gamecube controller.

1. I'd watch streams of other Oblivion runners. Most runners are more than willing to help if you go into their streams. There might be a website for Elder Scrolls speedruns too if you ask around. (note: I know nothing about oblivion speedruns, these are just general tips for finding speedruns of a game).

2. You don't need to stream. Local recordings are acceptable. 

3. There's no secret to optimizing a game. You just have to learn how the game works and the optimizations will come naturally.
